discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moire quantum matter)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group, using precise tear-and-stack fabrication of ultraclean hBN-encapsulated devices, discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in exactly this system. The twist angle thus became a new, continuously tunable parameter of quantum matter. This work founded the field of moire materials, now yielding orbital ferromagnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states, strange-metal transport and fractional Chern insulators in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide superlattices. Its lasting impact is methodological as much as conceptual: a single gate-tunable device now accesses phase diagrams once requiring many chemically distinct crystals. Laboratories worldwide, including in India, have adopted this platform, transforming how experimental condensed-matter physics is done.
